dek: Bus cameras, a $9 toll and record rents: what it really costs to live in New York in 2026.

slides.label: The curb
slides.text: NYC has about *3 million* street parking spots, and only about 80,000 are metered. New bus and bike lanes are taking more: *61* on 116th St, close to *300* on University Ave.

slides.label: The cameras
slides.text: Cameras on MTA buses now ticket *double-parking* and blocked bus stops on *62 routes*. Fines start at $50 and climb to $250.

slides.label: The tickets
slides.text: In one year: *1.1 million* bus-camera tickets for double-parking and blocking stops. Of 1,410 drivers who appealed, only *48* won.

slides.label: The toll
slides.text: It costs *$9* to drive into Manhattan below 60th St at peak hours. Traffic is down 11%, and the toll is set to rise in *2028*.

slides.label: The garage
slides.text: A monthly garage spot near Central Park can run *$1,400*. That's close to the typical *one-bedroom rent* across the US.

slides.label: The rent
slides.text: Manhattan's median rent hit a record *$5,295* a month. Stabilized rents are frozen, but market-rate tenants get *no relief*.

slides.label: The sidewalk
slides.text: Overdose deaths fell 28%, but NYC still loses someone *every 4 hours*. On one March night, *4,991* people slept outside or in the subways.

slides.label: The other side
slides.text: The city says camera routes run up to *30% faster* with 20% fewer collisions. Faster buses, and still *nowhere to stop*.

caption_instagram:
Living in New York in 2026 costs more at every turn, and the street itself has less room for all of it.

Cameras on MTA buses now ticket double-parking on 62 routes, even if you're just running the groceries upstairs. In one year they wrote more than 1.1 million tickets for double-parking and blocking bus stops, and only 48 of 1,410 appeals won. New bus and bike lanes are taking spots, the $9 congestion toll is set to rise in 2028, and a garage spot near Central Park can cost about as much as a one-bedroom apartment in the rest of the country. Manhattan's median rent just hit a record $5,295.

The city's side: camera routes run up to 30% faster with 20% fewer collisions, and traffic in the toll zone is down 11%.

Bus cameras: SAFER streets or CASH GRAB? Pick one.

New York's curb is being rebuilt, and residents are paying for the transition.

In fiscal 2026, MTA bus cameras issued more than 1.1 million tickets for double-parking and blocking bus stops. Bus and bike lanes are replacing parking, the $9 congestion toll is set to rise in 2028, and Manhattan's median rent hit a record $5,295. The city points to buses up to 30% faster with 20% fewer collisions on camera routes.

For small businesses and delivery operators, the open question is where a legal two-minute stop fits. DOT data says loading zones cut double-parking by up to 70%, yet they remain scarce.
